parts.t: Neighbourhood guide · City of Chilliwack · Eastern Hillsides
Eastern Hillsides is an MLS® sub-area name in the City of Chilliwack. The City doesn’t publish a boundary for it. The closest official description is the Eastern Hillsides Neighbourhood Plan area.

The plan area is in the southeast part of Chilliwack, about 8 kilometres from downtown, and covers approximately 1,340 hectares. It is bounded to the west by the Ryder Lake uplands, to the south by Lookout Ridge and Elk Mountain, to the east by the Cascades in the Fraser Valley Regional District, and to the north by the Trans-Canada Highway and valley floor farmland.
The City classifies Eastern Hillsides as a “hillside neighbourhood” in its Official Community Plan neighbourhood structure.

blocks.text: Planning and flood notes for Eastern Hillsides

parts.t: Plans, zoning and flood rules can be different for each lot.

The Eastern Hillsides Neighbourhood Plan is now Schedule B4 of Official Community Plan Bylaw 2025, No. 5500. The plan document was prepared by the City Planning Department in May 2012 and updated in 2025.

The plan document records that the City adopted the Eastern Hillsides Comprehensive Development Plan in 1994, and that Hillside Development Guidelines and a Municipal Tree Management Regulation followed in 2008 and 2009.

Under the 2050 plan update, the plan’s land use designations were replaced with the City-wide Official Community Plan designations. The development cells and unit allocations still regulate how many units may be developed.

ALR: the plan’s site-capacity work used the Agricultural Land Reserve as a constraint, but published municipal records do not list a specific ALR parcel in the area. City-wide, 67% of Chilliwack’s land (17,322 hectares) is in the ALR, and the Fraser River valley bottom accounts for 14,000 hectares of that.
Slope: about 45% of the plan area has slopes over 30%. Five main watercourses and ravines cross it, and the plan identifies geotechnical hazard areas.

The Greenspace Plan names the lower Marble Hill Slide area (mainly City-owned properties) and the upper Marble Hill Slide area (private undevelopable lands) among its sub-community park locations for the Eastern Hillsides.
Flood: the plan area is hillside land above the valley floor, with valley floor farmland along its northern edge.

blocks.text: Before you buy in Eastern Hillsides

parts.t: Check the slope and the geotechnical report.
About 45% of the plan area is steeper than 30%, so ask the City and the seller for any geotechnical report on the lot.
Ask the City whether a watercourse or ravine setback affects the lot, and have the inspector check drainage.
Ask the City how the plan’s development cells and unit allocations affect what can be built nearby.
There is no school in the plan area, and SD33 is changing catchments in September 2027, so use the SD33 School Locator for the exact address.
Check how you will get around.
Published municipal records list no bus route into the plan area, so plan for a car or check BC Transit.
Check the roof, drainage, furnace, plumbing and wiring.

What parks and trails are in Eastern Hillsides?

The City’s directory lists Allan Creek Park (51314 Rowanna Cres), Forest Gate Park (51442 Allan Rd), Marble Hill Natural Area (7515 Marble Hill Rd) and the Chilliwack Community Forest (51642 Allan Rd), plus Allan Creek Trail and Elk Mountain Trail.
No City recreation centre is in the area. The nearest is Cheam Leisure Centre at 45501 Market Way.
The nearest library is the Chilliwack Library at 45860 First Avenue.
